title: Client Lifeline: Escalation & Mitigation Framework
body:
Purpose and scope:
This working playbook (Client Lifeline) outlines an operational approach to spotting renewal risk early, doing rapid triage, and escalating to the right partners — including an executive escalation track — when account health requires human intervention. It focuses on pragmatic, time-boxed mitigation plays that can be executed by success managers, solutions engineers, and executive sponsors to materially increase renewal probability.

Principles:
- Fail fast: surface risk early with low-friction signals and act within the first 30 days of detection.
- Proportional escalation: match the intensity of the response to the magnitude and probability of churn.
- Combine data + human judgment: metrics trigger triage; conversations determine root cause.
- Time-boxed interventions: every mitigation play has an owner, a 1-2 week target, and a measurable acceptance criteria.

Early-warning signals (triage priority order):
1) Usage collapse: >40% month-over-month DAU/MAU drop or >50% drop in key feature calls in 14 days.
2) Billing or procurement stalls: invoicing disputes, delayed PO, or contract negotiations exceeding 45 days before renewal.
3) Support friction: rising page count (>3 P1s in 30 days) or open high-severity bugs blocking core workflows.
4) Product-level regressions: recent model quality regressions on customer test prompts or increased hallucination reports.
5) Engagement signals: missed QBRs, repeated reschedules, or lack of response to outreach for >21 days.
6) Commercial cues: seat reassignments, public layoffs, or budget freezes mentioned in calls/emails.

Triage checklist (within 48 hours of signal):
- Pull: account health dashboard, billing status, recent support tickets, last 4 weeks of usage logs.
- Quick root hypothesis: product quality, adoption, cost, contractual, security/compliance, or organizational change.
- Customer contact: schedule a 30-min alignment call within 72 hours. Use this script: "We saw X, want to understand impact on your goals, and propose short fixes we can try in the next 7–14 days."
- Severity score (0–10) and recommended track: self-service remediation (0–3), success-led plays (4–6), immediate exec escalation (7–10).

Escalation triggers (prompts to start executive track):
- Severity >= 8 OR
- Contract >= $250k ARR with risk of non-renewal within 90 days OR
- Billing/legal/regulatory dispute unresolved for >14 days OR
- Repeated P1 incidents impacting revenue or customer-facing production for >3 days OR
- Customer explicitly requests to pause or exit at contract end.

Stakeholder mapping (example roles and responsibilities):
- CSM (owner): day-to-day communications, coordinates fixes, owns 14-day mitigation plan.
- SE/PS: implements technical mitigations, creates short-term workarounds.
- Solutions Architect: scope for any immediate configuration changes or architecture notes.
- AE: commercial conversations, renewal negotiations, and PO follow-ups.
- Customer Success Leader (manager): approves resource allocation and escalates to executive sponsor.
- Executive Sponsor (VP/GM): engages customer execs, provides commercial concessions, and clears cross-org blockers.

Executive escalation cadence (template):
1) Internal sync (same day): CSM + SE + AE + CS leader, 30 min — share severity score, hypothesis, proposed mitigation, and asks of exec sponsor.
2) Partner with Executive Sponsor (within 48 hours): one-call prep to align on tone, concession policy, and desired outcome.
3) Customer exec touchpoint (within 72 hours): 30–45 min meeting with customer exec + our exec sponsor; aim is to align on critical outcomes and present time-boxed remediation.
4) Follow-up plan: 1-week checkpoint, 2-week technical deliverable, and 30-day business review.

Executive escalation email template (CS leader to Exec Sponsor):
Subject: Exec Escalation request — [Account] — renewal risk (severity X)
Body: Hello [Exec Name],
We need your quick help with [Account, ARR $X, renewal date: YYYY-MM-DD]. Observed issues: [list 3 bullet points with metrics].
Impact: [customer success metric, revenue risk, timeline].
Ask: join one 30–45 min meeting with their [title] to align on ASAP fixes + help unblock procurement. Proposed time slots: [3 options].
Prep: CSM will share a 1-pager and a 7–14 day mitigation plan before the call.

Mitigation playbook (fast-fail plays, each 7–14 day):
- Micro-saves (CSM led, 0–3 days): targeted walkthrough, usage nudges, tailored runbook, offer quick-win configuration changes. Acceptance criteria: 10% usage rebound or customer acknowledgement of resumed progress.
- Temporary concessions (AE + CS Leader, 3–7 days): extended trial, limited credit, or deferral of a charge to regain trust. Acceptance: written agreement to continued evaluation.
- Rapid engineering response (SE/Platform, 3–10 days): hotfix, prioritized bug patch, or temporary configuration to restore SLAs. Acceptance: bug fixed in staging and validated by customer.
- Dedicated enablement sprint (PS, 7–14 days): 1-week onboarding/enablement focused on key personas. Acceptance: attendees complete checklist and show usage lift on target workflows.
- Migration/architecture remediation (Solutions + Eng, 7–21 days): scope and backlog of long-term fixes. Acceptance: roadmap and milestone commitment signed by both sides.

Decision matrix (go/no-go within 14 days):
- If acceptance criteria met for core mitigation plays -> continue standard renewal process and track outcome in QBR.
- If acceptance partially met and product fixes in progress -> extend an interim term (90 days) + checkpoint.
- If no progress and severity stays >=8 -> escalate to commercial options (discount, short renewal, or disengagement plan) and prepare executive risk memo.

Example micro-play: "Token Cost Relief + Guided Prompts"
- Trigger: sudden spike in tokens used with no comms and usage drop in critical flows.
- Action: AE approves a temporary cost credit for next 30 days while CSM runs a 2-week guided prompt optimization series with customer engineers.
- Owner: AE (credit), CSM (program), SE (prompt guidance).
- Success: cost normalized and key flows return to 80% prior baseline.

Post-save stabilization & learnings (30–60 days):
- Conduct a stabilization QBR focused on measurable goals and agreed playbook updates.
- Document root causes, time-to-resolution, and recommended product or process changes.
- Convert the incident into a renewal narrative: evidence of improvement + executive involvement reduces churn risk.

Artifacts to prepare for escalation call (CSM must assemble):
- 1-page Impact summary (metrics, timeline, top 3 asks).
- Short remediation plan (owners, milestones, and acceptance criteria).
- Recent support log and sample error traces.
- Customer org chart + procurement timeline.

Metrics to track in the account scorecard (weekly) after mitigation starts:
- Usage delta (weekly % change)
- Open critical tickets (# and age)
- Net retention risk score (0–100) with rationale text
- Commercial timeline (PO/contract stage)
- Exec touchpoints (dates and outcomes)

Open questions & next steps (working items):
- Define financial thresholds for automatic exec sponsor assignment (proposed: >=$250k ARR).
- Template library: add 3 exec email variants (tone: urgency, partnership, remediation offer).
- Measure impact: track closed-loop outcomes for 50 triaged accounts to calculate playbook lift.

Notes to self / working assumptions:
- This is a living playbook. Keep plays short and reversible.
- Prioritize customer trust and transparency; escalate only with clear asks.
- We expect ~30% of exec escalations to convert to renewals when paired with measurable product fixes and documented stabilization.
